notes: Access: robots.txt (fetched via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124, 200 OK) has a named 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Crawl-delay: 5' block with NO Disallow -> explicitly permitted, paced accordingly. Direct HTTP (curl_cffi, chrome124 impersonation) returned Akamai 'Access Denied' 403 on every macys.com URL tried, including the roster URL id=22672 and URLs verified working in the prior Home-Decor pass (archive c74) -- access conditions changed since that pass. Playwright headless (same UA) also got 403/Access Denied from Akamai. Escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (Tier 3) per brief: navigating in the real Chrome session passed Akamai's JS challenge automatically on first load; all data below was extracted from that authenticated browser session. Roster URL /shop/home?id=22672 and /shop/pet-shop both redirect to the generic homepage (dead/renumbered), so the Pet department was located via the homepage footer link 'See All Pet Supplies' -> /shop/interests-activities/pets?id=197851. That root Pets landing page shows a non-exact '(500+)' header and is a mixed Dog+Cat+Small-Animal roll-up -- used only as navigation root, never as a leaf qty, per the Home Accents caveat pattern from the prior pass. QTY METHOD: same Nuxt SSR devalue payload approach verified in the prior pass -- each category page embeds a <script type=application/json> containing a flattened array; the raw text has a literal '"totalResults":<idx>' (and resultsPerPage/numberOfPages) whose <idx> indexes into the parsed array to give the real number. Cross-checked on every single category below: ceil(totalResults/resultsPerPage) == numberOfPages passed on all ~23 samples (resultsPerPage was stable at 60 throughout). TAXONOMY: site exposes a real 2-tier nav -- Pets > {Cat(id=325959), Dog(id=325958), Small Animal(id=363373)} -- each with its own set of category pills (breadcrumb URL segments, e.g. /pets/dog/beds?id=328260), which is what the rows below are built from. Small Animal has no further pills/children (leaf, 88 items, title 'Small Animal & Bird Accessories'; one sampled item, a generic garden hardware-cloth wire mesh, looked like nav contamination but the other 87 sampled titles were genuine small-animal/bird pet products, so the node was kept as-is). DEDUP: Dog 'Carriers & Crates' (id=363363, totalResults=283) and Cat 'Carriers & Crates' (id=328267, totalResults=283) are the SAME listing -- identical totalResults and identical first-6 product hrefs/order verified on both URLs. Kept one row under Dog, dropped the Cat duplicate (explained here per the brief's merge rule). All other Dog vs Cat sibling pairs (Beds, Clothing, Collars, Feeders, Food&Treats, Grooming, Health&Wellness) were checked and have different totalResults and/or different first-page product sets, so kept separate. GAP-FILL FROM FACETS: the pill taxonomy has no 'Toys' or 'Litter' or 'Waste/Hygiene' node at all, even though the brief lists these as Tier-1 decisive categories, so real navigation was checked further -- each species page also exposes a 'Pet Accessories' facet whose values are themselves clickable PLP links with the URL shape /pets/<species>/Pet_accessories/<value>?id=<speciesId>. Verified this facet is genuinely species-scoped (not a shared/universal count) by cross-checking 'Pet Waste Bags & Cleaning' under Dog scope (42) vs Cat scope (19) -- different totals, confirms real scoping, not a display artifact. Added from this facet, one row per species, after sampling first-page titles to confirm a clean single-purpose bucket: 'Toys' (Dog Pet_accessories/'Pet Toys'=273, sampled titles were all genuine dog toys/balls/plush chews; Cat Pet_accessories/'Pet Toys'=122), 'Cat Litter & Supplies' (Cat only, 14 -- litter boxes/trays, genuine Tier-1 hygiene, no Dog equivalent exists), 'Waste Bags & Cleaning' (Dog=42, Cat=19 -- poop bags/scoopers/pee pads/waste stations, genuine Tier-1 hygiene, sampled titles confirmed, not covered by any pill). EXCLUDED facet values (checked, then dropped to avoid double-counting against the pill categories already captured): 'Pet Storage' (Dog=24 -- sampled titles were all elevated dog-feeding stations with storage drawers, i.e. already inside the 'Feeders & Bowls' pill population, not a distinct bucket); 'Pet Mats' (Dog=78 -- sampled titles were a mixed cross-cut of a dog car-seat cover, pee pads (already in Waste Bags & Cleaning), a feeding mat (already in Feeders & Bowls) and a crate mat (already in Crates/Gates/Pens) -- no clean single owner, dropped per the 'generic product types need a clear, non-overlapping parent' rule); 'Gates & Containment' (redundant with the Crates/Gates/Pens and Doors & Gates pill nodes); 'Pet Tech' and 'Carries' (n=1, ambiguous/negligible, not evaluated further). Also excluded as out of scope entirely: nothing found under Kids & Baby/Toys top-level nav resembling live-animal pet care (checked and confirmed unrelated, that's the Toys R Us toy-department nav item, not pets). Two open-policy flags applied per brief section 3: Food & Treats nodes (genuine consumables, flagged not dropped) and Health & Wellness nodes (post-surgery recovery suits/cone collars/joint & digestive supplements -- genuine veterinary/medical category, sampled and confirmed, flagged not dropped).
